chapter: Harlem musicians and the road with Armstrong
title: Armstrong never knew where the band was playing and slept on buses
summary: Armstrong left all band business to Russell and Glaser and slept soundly on the bus while Holmes could not.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Well, what kind of relationship did Louis have with the band? Did he in any way...?

Louis got up there and blew his horn. He had nothin' to say to the band as far as running the band was concerned. He wasn't interested in what the band's business was. Luis Russell was running the band...and Joe Glaser. Joe Glaser run everything. See, all the orders come from Joe Glaser. And Louis, he didn't bother himself with the band. Louis didn't know where he was working the next night. People would come up to the bandstand and ask, "Oh, Louis, where are you playing tomorrow night?" And Louis would have to ask somebody in the band. "Where we at tomorrow night?" He didn't know.

He never knew. He didn't care. You know, when he got through work he would get dressed and get in the bus and go to sleep in the bus -- and he could sleep on the bus, too. It would make me so mad! He would sit across from me, and I could never sleep on a bus... I'd be awake two and three nights at a time. And he'd come in the bus, and right away [SNORE]...and sleep the whole trip. When we'd get there, he's all right, he feels good. I couldn't sleep, and I was very nervous. And when I get out of the bus and get on the bandstand, I'm ready for a bed. And it was all... I'd sit on the bandstand and I couldn't keep my eyes open. But I
get in the bus and I'm wide-awake, I can't sleep.
